title: add-burst-aware-token-cost-hedger-and-contextual-alert-policy
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Introduce a burst-aware token-cost hedger service plus a contextual per-tenant dashboard and an adaptive alert policy. Hedger reduces noisy alerts during short token surges and provides suggested fallback actions (model fallback, quota bump, quiet window). Includes sampling and cardinality controls to limit telemetry cost.
description: Motivation: We see recurring false-positive token-cost alerts when high short-lived bursts (e.g., chatbots hitting a prompt loop or synthetic traffic) spike per-tenant token consumption for a few seconds. Existing rules fire aggressively and shift on-call attention away from real regressions. This PR adds a lightweight 'Token Cost Hedger' service that detects burst patterns, annotates traces, and provides a graded alerting adapter that reduces noise while preserving SLO sensitivity. Changes in this PR: 1) telemetry/hedger: new hedger service that ingests summarized per-invocation token counts and maintains a short epoch-based baseline per-tenant+model. Detects burst anomalies using an exponentially-weighted moving baseline and a burst-window score; exposes hedger decisions via traces and metrics. 2) tracing: add token_hedger.evaluate span and hedger decision tags to invocation traces so downstream tools can join hedger annotations to existing spans. 3) alerts: adaptive alert policy token_cost_burst.yaml that uses hedger.score and quiet-window gating before escalating alerts. 4) dashboard: observability/dashboards/token-hedger.json with a per-tenant sparkline, burst-score heatmap, waterfall token-cost decomposition (kernel queue, generation, streaming). 5) docs: docs/observability/hedger.md describing configuration knobs (window size, sensitivity, fallback suggestions). 6) tests: hedger unit tests and a small integration harness that replays synthetic bursts. Rollout plan: deploy hedger as opt-in behind feature flag (.observability.hedger.enabled = true) for 7 days on a shadowing mode (emit metrics/trace tags but do not influence alert routing), then enable gating for canary tenants (5%) before turning on platform-wide. Backout plan: feature flag off; alerts fall back to previous rule. Design notes: hedger keeps only ephemeral per-tenant state (TTL 10m) and applies reservoir sampling for high-cardinality tenants to keep cardinality bounded. Hedger exposes three primary metrics: hedger.epoch_baseline_tokens, hedger.burst_score, hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts. Privacy/security: hedger operates on aggregated counts and tenant IDs; no request payloads stored. See linked linear tasks for evaluation and SLO calibration. CI status: initial lint failure due to docs formatting; fixed in a follow-up commit. All tests green on final run. Merge outcome: squash-merged to main.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: This is promising—can you quantify the expected reduction in alert noise? Also worried about unbounded cardinality if we tag traces per-tenant. Could we add reservoir sampling?

Aisha Raman (author): Added reservoir sampling and a per-tenant cardinality cap; updated docs to call out TTL and sampling behavior. I ran a 48h synthetic replay and saw ~72% reduction in short-lived alert churn on noisy tenants (measured in dev replay).
Priya Shah: Please add a small experiment to ensure SLO detection power isn't reduced for multi-minute regressions. Also request an e2e-observability job covering hedger gating logic.

Aisha Raman: Added e2e-observability tests that simulate sustained regressions vs spikes; hedger only suppresses when burst_score > threshold and duration < burst_window. Added metric hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts for monitoring. Tests added and CI updated.
Ethan Liu: Approve after addressing cardinality and adding the runbook section for incident response. Left one minor nit about naming hedger.metric -> hedger.epoch_baseline_tokens.
Priya Shah: Approved; e2e run passed on canary tenants.
notes_on_rollout: Start in shadow mode for 7 days, enable gating for 5% canary tenants, then ramp to 100% over 48h. Monitor hedger.noise_suppressed_alerts and hedger.burst_score distributions; rollback if suppressed_alerts for high-severity SLO violations > 1% for two consecutive 10m windows.
impact_analysis: Low operational risk; hedger only annotates traces and emits metrics in shadow mode. When gating is enabled it will suppress noisy alerts but keeps a fallback path to notify on sustained regressions. Telemetry cost increase is bounded by reservoir sampling and 10m TTL. Expected benefit: reduce pager churn from short-lived bursts and improve signal-to-noise for oncall.
